subject: Dedicated fleet tiering & SKU playbook for Mosaic Analytics
thread_text:
From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@mosaic.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 6 Jun 2027 15:32:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity ask — mixed workloads and peak SLAs

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick follow-up on the committed Dedicated capacity conversation: Mosaic runs a mix of workloads — high-concurrency embedding generation for search (short contexts, heavy batching), and low-concurrency long-context QA/summarization pipelines (70k tokens, few concurrent requests). We need guidance on a SKU mix that keeps (1) 99th percentile latency for QA under 450ms per token at burst, (2) embeddings throughput of ~8k reqs/min, and (3) predictable monthly committed spend.

Can Redwood propose a tiering policy (primary/secondary SKUs) and notes on memory vs perf tradeoffs for H100 / A100 / L4 that we can show to procurement? I attached our simplified capacity model.

Appreciate any quick thoughts — we plan to decide on reserved capacity by next week.

— Alex
Head of ML Platform
Mosaic Analytics

Alex — thanks for the context and for the attachment. Looping in Marissa and Dev for SKU and ops guidance. High level from my side: we typically recommend a hybrid fleet for that profile — H100s for the long-context, high-memory models (LLMs > 40B or 70k token sequences), A100s for the 7–40B family where NVLink helps multi-GPU servings, and L4s for embeddings/high-concurrency cheap inference. But the exact split depends on the model family you lock to and quantization headroom. 

Marissa/Dev — can you review the attached capacity model and propose a tiering policy (Primary = reserved; Secondary = burst) plus a simple cost delta per token for each SKU? High priority: ensuring the 99p latency objective for QA.

Neha
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — mixed workloads and peak SLAs

Folks — reviewed Mosaic's workbook and sketched a recommended fleet-tiering policy. Summary first, then notes and an ops checklist.

Summary recommendation (targeted at Mosaic's SLA and throughput):
- Primary tier (Reserved capacity): mix of H100-80GB (25% of reserved GPUs) + A100-80GB (50% of reserved GPUs) + L4 (25% of reserved GPUs). Rationale: keep H100s for memory-bound 70k token sessions where single-GPU memory and high FP16/TF32 perf matter; A100s for the majority of mid-size models and for NVLink sharded runs; L4s for embeddings / short context microservices to minimize $/embedding.
- Secondary tier (Burst/On-demand): additional A100s + cheaper L4 pools in another region for cost-effective bursting and to satisfy peak embedding spikes. H100 burst only if long-context pipelines exceed reserved capacity.

Detailed tradeoffs and operational notes:
1) Memory vs performance:
   - H100-80GB: best for very large models or long sequences due to large VRAM and faster tensor core kernels; yields higher per-token throughput for long-context workloads and enables larger KV cache. Cost: highest per-GPU-hour.
   - A100-80GB: sweet spot for 7–30B models and sharded setups (NVLink/PCIe); lower cost than H100 but can require multi-GPU orchestration for very large seq lengths. Good for batched mid-size inference.
   - L4 (48GB effective inference optimized variant): designed for dense small-context tasks and embeddings; excellent cost per embedding; not ideal for >30k token single sessions.

2) Quantization & model variants:
   - Recommend pushing 4-bit + mixed-precision quantization for A100/L4 where model quality tolerates it — yields 1.8–2.6x throughput improvement and reduces memory footprint enabling fewer H100s for edge cases.
   - For H100-hosted large models keep at least one full-precision / 16-bit variant for clients sensitive to quality/regression. Canary rollout with Redwood Optimize to measure regression on Mosaic's eval set.

3) Latency SLOs and batching strategies:
   - Long-context QA: prefer single-request streaming on H100 with small micro-batches (1–4) to control 99p latency. Use KV caching for repeated context prefixes.
   - Embeddings: allow larger batch windows on L4 with continuous batching; set a separate embedding route with tight priority for spikes.

4) Host-level considerations:
   - NVLink topology: for A100 clusters configure nodes with full NVLink for cross-GPU KV/cache transfers. This dramatically lowers tail latency for sharded generation.
   - Memory oversubscription: avoid swap-based oversubscription; prefer adding H100 units rather than memory ballooning.

5) Cost modeling (order-of-magnitude):
   - H100-80GB: ~3.5x A100 cost per GPU-hour; per-token cost for long-context generation often lower because fewer cross-GPU calls, but absolute reserved cost high.
   - A100-80GB: baseline for most balanced workloads.
   - L4: ~0.25–0.35x A100 cost for embeddings; best $/embedding.

Ops checklist for onboarding Mosaic (minimum viable reserved config):
- Reserve: 6 A100-80GB, 2 H100-80GB, 8 L4 instances tied to an embedding pool.
- Autoscale headroom: +40% burst capacity in A100/L4; H100 burst optional via cloud on-demand.
- Canary: deploy 1 H100 and 2 A100 replicas behind canary for QA pipeline; run Redwood Optimize evals for 72h.
- Telemetry: enable token-level cost & 99p latency dashboards; hook Mosaic's tracing ids.

I'll attach quick numbers in a spreadsheet (per your workbook) and a sample SLA-friendly rollout plan.

— Dev
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Alex — echo Dev's technical plan. A couple procurement-friendly notes to include in the proposal and next steps for contracting: 

- Pricing packaging: we typically present a two-tier reserved commitment: (1) Core Reserved (6 months min) covers the Primary tier above with committed discount; (2) Flex Burst pool billed monthly with prioritized capacity at a blended overage rate. We can lock a blended committed rate for A100s/H100s and a lower separate rate for L4s.
- Term suggestions: 12-month reserved with quarterly check-ins and capacity rebalancing clauses. Include a clause for spillover bursting into Redwood Dedicated marketplace at pre-agreed rates to avoid unpredictable on-demand spikes.
- Procurement ask from Mosaic: confirmation of model family and % of inference served by embeddings vs long-context pipelines (Dev's workbook helps).

If this looks OK I'll draft a short SOW and committed capacity term sheet.

— Marissa
Sr. Sales Lead, Dedicated Accounts
Redwood Inference

- I'll confirm the model families tomorrow (we have a mix of internally distilled 70B and 13B transformer variants; embeddings are a separate microservice).
- Can you include the recommended quantization guardrails and a short regression test template we can run during canary?

Next step: Marissa — SOW + committed rate table; Dev — brief quantization/regression template; Neha — I'll set a procurement review for Friday.

Thanks again — Alex
